target_customer: Dentists and dental service organizations such as Pacific Dental Services
problem: Tooth preparation for crowns and similar procedures takes long chair time, needs x-rays for diagnosis, and varies with the dentist's hand skill.
business_model: Hardware plus software dental robotics system sold to dental practices (pre-commercial, not FDA cleared)
product_category: Dental robotics, OCT imaging and AI diagnosis

founders.name: Chris Ciriello
founders.background_notes: YC page bio credits him with the biomarker thesis, first in-motion OCT, AI OCT models and the first human automated dental crown prep. Education and employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Scott Phillips
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Neocis
competitors.what: Yomi, an FDA-cleared robot that guides dental implant surgery
competitors.traction_then: FDA clearance in 2016 per later coverage; sources opened do not give 2020 customer counts

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines a new imaging modality (in-motion OCT that sees inside teeth), AI diagnosis and a surgical robot cutting teeth autonomously, with a regulatory path the CEO said was about five years from FDA submission as of 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware, clinical data and regulatory clearance are slow to replicate, and the first human automated crown prep in 2024 gave a lead. Dental chain investor Pacific Dental Services adds a distribution link.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found building autonomous tooth cutting at founding; Neocis automated implant guidance only. No acquisition reported in sources opened.

market_need_then: The company cites a $452B dental industry and underserved populations with limited access to dental care; dentists face long procedure times and x-ray based diagnosis. Direct demand evidence from 2020 was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses perceptive.io per YC page; domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: clinical and technical; site stresses safety and that products are prototypes not FDA cleared

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources. Dates inferred from trademark filings (PERCEPTIVE DENTAL filed 2023-09) and the 2024 announcements using the new name.

branding.community_and_virality: The July 2024 first automated dental procedure drew wide press and the Ed Zuckerberg investor angle, but no fan community was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Rename to a generic word with some press from the 2024 milestone; no evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Perceptive stayed in long-horizon R&D after YC W2020, raising a $15M Series A led by Pacific Dental Services in 2022 and a $30M round in 2024 after exiting stealth with the first fully automated human crown prep. The regulatory path is years away, so commercial outcome is unproven; capital from a dental chain suggests early distribution interest.
notes: Series A of $15M in 2022-10 is from an aggregator article and a search summary naming Pacific Dental Services as lead; the YC page links a TechCrunch article that is actually about a different company. The 2024 $30M is labeled other because sources do not label it. Caplight shows a Series B dated 2025-01 and $77M total, unverified and not recorded. Investor list for 2024 is from SD Magazine as summarized in search. The company site was opened but its team page was not available. Founder education and prior employers not found.
